sources.title: Enable Copilot case and conversation summaries
Configure Copilot features in the help pane
Configure context variables for AI agents
Understand skill matching in unified routing

notes.title: Give representatives the right Copilot assistance
notes.body:
Start with the task: finding a knowledge-based answer and recapping a conversation are different needs. Configure the help pane for questions; configure conversation summaries for a recap. Then enable the appropriate features in the representatives’ experience profile rather than assuming global setup gives every group identical access.

Custom security roles also need the documented Copilot privileges.

For standalone Contact Center, conversation summaries can cover chat and transcribed voice. An administrator can trigger them when someone joins, at the end, or on demand. Representatives can copy a summary or give feedback; creating a case from it additionally requires case management and the enabled action.

For example, a consultation needs a useful recap, while a product-policy question needs suitable published knowledge. Validate both workflows with the intended profile.

notes.title: Scope voice-agent variables before sharing context
notes.body:
For the native standalone integration, a context variable and its Copilot Studio counterpart need matching names and compatible types. A global variable is accessible across topics in one user session; it is not a permanent customer record. Use a Set variable value node when the agent must assign a value itself.

For external values, enable the global and external-source usage settings. Keep the channel’s limitations explicit: Contact Center IVR does not support the external-variable timeout setting described for other scenarios. Do not design voice recovery around that timer.

For example, retain a caller’s selected service category across topics, then pass the relevant context at escalation. This transfers conversation context, not proof that an arbitrary value authenticates the caller.

notes.title: Separate work enrichment from representative assignment
notes.body:
Classification enriches a work item; assignment selects an eligible representative. Keep these responsibilities visible when troubleshooting. A useful classification attribute can be reused by queue-routing or prioritization rules, instead of repeating the same business test in several places.

Ruleset order matters. Classification runs before route-to-queue evaluation, and a later classification ruleset can consume an earlier ruleset’s output. Within one classification ruleset, a matching item passes processing to the next ruleset.

For example, derive an urgency category once, then use it downstream. Separately inspect the queue’s assignment method and representative eligibility. A classification result does not mean that a suitable representative is immediately available; automated assignment retries when it cannot find one.

notes.title: Treat skill eligibility and workload limits separately
notes.body:
An exact skill match requires the attached skills at sufficient proficiency. With standard assignment, presence and available capacity also matter. A queue using custom assignment needs its own skill conditions; the workstream’s default skill algorithm does not supply those conditions automatically.

Capacity profiles describe workload limits. Assignment blocking can stop further automatic work when a profile reaches its limit, even if another profile has room. A supervisor’s manual assignment can exceed configured capacity, so the limit is not an absolute ban on every assignment path.

For example, an unassigned language-specific conversation calls for an eligibility check, while unexpected extra manually assigned work calls for a capacity-path check. Do not treat these as the same fault.

cards.prompt: Which conversation types can Copilot summarize in standalone Contact Center?
cards.explanation: The conversation-summary setup targets a conversation recap, distinct from a case summary.

cards.prompt: Where can a representative find a saved summary for a closed conversation?
cards.answer: Open the conversation from Activities and use its Summary tab.
cards.explanation: The closed conversation remains a place to review its generated recap.

cards.prompt: Which Copilot filter lets representatives choose knowledge filters themselves in Ask a question?
cards.explanation: Enable its filter status so it appears in the help pane.

cards.prompt: Does a Copilot Studio global variable retain its value across all future customer sessions?
cards.answer: No. Its scope spans topics within one user session.
cards.explanation: A global variable is session-scoped, not permanent customer storage; clearing or resetting variables can also remove its value.

cards.prompt: Copilot is configured and all representatives have the required security privileges. Only the escalation team should receive the selected Copilot features. Which configuration should define that team's feature access?

options.text: Enable the selected features in a custom experience profile and assign it to that team.
Enable the features in the default experience profile assigned to every representative.
Enable recording of Copilot interactions for the escalation team.
Apply a preset knowledge filter for the team's subject area.

cards.answer: Enable the selected features in a custom experience profile and assign it to that team.
cards.explanation: Experience profiles determine the Copilot features available to assigned representatives. A shared default profile does not isolate the team; recording captures interactions, and knowledge filters restrict response content rather than feature access.

cards.prompt: A native standalone voice agent needs the caller's phone number in several topics. Where should it first copy Activity.From.Name?

options.text: Into a topic variable in Conversation Start, then reference it directly from every topic.
Into a global variable in Conversation Start.
Into a global variable in the later topic where the number is first needed.
Into a separate topic variable by reading Activity.From.Name again in each later topic.

cards.answer: Into a global variable in Conversation Start.
cards.explanation: Activity.From.Name is available only in Conversation Start. Copy it there into a global variable for subsequent topics. A topic-only variable lacks direct cross-topic scope; waiting to read the system variable in later topics loses the documented access point.

cards.prompt: What are unified routing's two main stages?
cards.explanation: Classification enriches the work item; assignment prioritizes and matches work to representatives.

cards.prompt: Can a later work classification ruleset use an attribute set by an earlier ruleset?
cards.explanation: Order the rulesets so the producer runs before the consumer.

cards.prompt: In advanced round robin, is assignment order maintained globally or per queue?
cards.explanation: Membership in multiple queues can therefore lead to consecutive assignments from different queues.

cards.prompt: Does Exact Match require proficiency to equal the required rating exactly?
cards.answer: No. A matching representative can meet or exceed the required proficiency.
cards.explanation: All required skills must still be satisfied.

cards.prompt: Two conditions match within one work classification ruleset. The first rule sets priority; a later rule would set severity, but severity remains unset. Both classifications must run. What should you change?

options.text: Put the severity rule first and keep both rules in this ruleset.
Move the severity rule into a subsequent work classification ruleset.
Leave the rules unchanged and rely on the next assignment cycle to evaluate the severity rule.
Put route-to-queue rules before work classification to make every classification rule run.

cards.answer: Move the severity rule into a subsequent work classification ruleset.
cards.explanation: After the first matching classification rule, evaluation proceeds to the next ruleset. Reordering the two rules still runs only the first match; later assignment does not rerun skipped classification rules.

cards.prompt: A supervisor manually assigns an extra conversation beyond a representative's configured capacity. Automatic assignments respect the limit. Which explanation best fits the documented behavior?

options.text: The work item limit is only enforced when an Exact Match skill algorithm is selected.
The representative must have lost their capacity-profile association.
Manual assignment can override the configured capacity limit.
Any extra conversation proves that the profile's automatic assignment limit is invalid.

cards.answer: Manual assignment can override the configured capacity limit.
cards.explanation: Microsoft documents supervisor manual assignment as an override of configured capacity. The scenario supplies no evidence of a missing profile or invalid automatic limit, and the capacity override is not defined by choosing Exact Match.

questions.prompt: A standalone Contact Center pilot has Copilot enabled and the intended experience profile assigned. Representatives with the standard role can use it, but a custom-role group cannot. What should the administrator check next?
questions.answer: Check the custom role's required Copilot privileges.
questions.explanation: The working standard-role group and confirmed profile isolate the next check to the failing custom role's Copilot privileges.

options.text: Re-enable Copilot for the environment, without inspecting the custom role.
Check the custom role's required Copilot privileges.
Reassign the same experience profile that the scenario already confirms is correct.
Enable recording of representative interactions with Copilot.

optionExplanations.a: Standard-role users already succeed, so repeating environment enablement does not address the role-specific difference.
optionExplanations.b: Custom security roles must include the documented Copilot privileges.
optionExplanations.c: The intended profile is already assigned; repeating that assignment does not check the missing permission layer.
optionExplanations.d: Interaction recording captures usage and feedback rather than granting the custom role access.

questions.prompt: A standalone Contact Center team wants an automatic chat recap when a colleague joins a consultation, before the conversation ends. Which conversation-summary trigger meets that timing requirement?
questions.answer: When a representative joins the conversation
questions.explanation: Configure the join event rather than relying on end-of-conversation or manual generation.

options.text: Only when the conversation ends
Only when a representative requests a summary
Only when the case closes
When a representative joins the conversation

optionExplanations.a: This waits until the wrong event.
optionExplanations.c: The requirement concerns a live conversation, not case closure.
optionExplanations.d: The join trigger includes consultation and transfer scenarios.

questions.prompt: For Ask a question using the organization's knowledge base, an administrator needs the same fixed topic restriction applied in the background. It must not depend on the current record or be selectable by representatives. Which filter type fits?
questions.explanation: Use a preset filter for the fixed restriction; ensure matching knowledge content exists.

options.text: Preset filter
Representative filter
Automated filter driven by current-record values
Enable the organization's knowledge base without defining filter conditions

optionExplanations.a: Preset conditions apply the fixed restriction in the background.
optionExplanations.b: These expose filtering choices to representatives, contrary to the requirement.
optionExplanations.c: This uses current-record context, which the requirement excludes.
optionExplanations.d: Choosing a knowledge source alone does not define the requested topic restriction.

questions.prompt: A Copilot Studio voice agent must accept serviceCategory from the native Contact Center integration and reuse it across topics. Its name and data type already match the external value. Which TWO Usage settings are required? Choose two.
questions.answer: Global (any topic can access) External sources can set values
questions.explanation: These settings provide scope and external initialization; they do not imply that IVR supports variable timeouts.

options.text: Restrict the variable to its current topic
Global (any topic can access)
Prevent external sources from changing values
External sources can set values

optionExplanations.a: Topic-only scope cannot meet the cross-topic requirement.
optionExplanations.b: Global scope allows other topics to use it.
optionExplanations.c: This contradicts receiving the external value.
optionExplanations.d: This permits the integration to supply the value.

questions.prompt: Several routing rules repeat the same static VIP-customer check, adding work to repeated assignment cycles. The result is also needed for queue selection. Which design best follows Microsoft's guidance?
questions.answer: Derive a reusable attribute during work classification.
questions.explanation: Compute stable categorization once, then consume it in route-to-queue and prioritization rules.

options.text: Repeat the full VIP check in every prioritization rule during each assignment cycle.
Evaluate VIP status only in route-to-queue rules and leave downstream prioritization to repeat the full check.
Derive a reusable attribute during work classification.
Add the full VIP check to a custom assignment rule and rely on it to populate the earlier queue-selection decision.

optionExplanations.a: This preserves the repeated processing that the design should reduce.
optionExplanations.b: Queue-only evaluation does not provide the shared classification value needed downstream.
optionExplanations.c: Microsoft recommends classifying static values once and reusing the attribute in route-to-queue and prioritization rules.
optionExplanations.d: Assignment occurs after queue routing; it cannot supply that earlier decision, and repeating complex assignment logic does not follow the guidance.

questions.prompt: A queue must assign work to the representative with the greatest available capacity among those satisfying every required skill and allowed presence. Which out-of-the-box configuration meets that requirement?
questions.explanation: The required ranking and strict eligibility must both be configured.

options.text: Highest capacity with Exact Match
Highest capacity with Closest Match
Advanced round robin with Exact Match
A custom alphabetical ordering

optionExplanations.a: Exact Match filters eligibility before capacity ordering.
optionExplanations.b: Closest Match orders by skill closeness rather than available capacity.
optionExplanations.c: Round robin uses assignment order, not greatest available capacity.
optionExplanations.d: Alphabetical order does not satisfy the capacity ranking requirement.

questions.prompt: A queue uses custom assignment rules that must be retained. The workstream's default is Exact Match, but the custom rules do not check skills. What change enforces the required skills without replacing those custom rules?
questions.answer: Add an explicit exact-skill condition to the custom assignment rules.
questions.explanation: The custom method overrides the workstream's default skill algorithm.

options.text: Switch the workstream's default algorithm to Closest Match while leaving the custom rules unchanged.
Attach required skills during classification but leave the custom assignment conditions unchanged.
Order custom assignment candidates by available capacity without adding a skill condition.
Add an explicit exact-skill condition to the custom assignment rules.

optionExplanations.a: Changing the workstream default does not add conditions to a custom assignment method.
optionExplanations.b: Attaching required skills describes the work, but custom assignment still needs a matching condition.
optionExplanations.c: Capacity ordering ranks candidates; it does not enforce the missing skill eligibility condition.
optionExplanations.d: Custom assignment needs its own skill conditions because it overrides the default skill algorithm.

questions.prompt: A capacity profile defaults to three chats. Experienced representatives should handle six, while trainees retain three. Reaching the applicable limit must block further automatic work across other profiles too. Which TWO changes meet these requirements? Choose two.
questions.answer: Set a custom limit of six for experienced representatives Enable Assignment blocking on the profile
questions.explanation: Combine individual workload limits with profile-level assignment blocking.

options.text: Raise the default limit for everyone to six
Set a custom limit of six for experienced representatives
Enable Assignment blocking on the profile
Add a second nonblocking profile for trainees

optionExplanations.a: That also raises the trainees' limit.
optionExplanations.b: Custom limits override the default for selected representatives.
optionExplanations.c: Blocking stops further automatic work when the applicable limit is met.
optionExplanations.d: Another nonblocking profile does not enforce the requested stop.
